cause_quote: When it added the 16-session warm-process cap, #69679 refused the turn with `throw new FailoverError("Too many Claude CLI live sessions are active.", { reason: "rate_limit", ... status: resolveFailoverStatus("rate_limit") })`, presenting a host limit as a provider 429.
user_saw: When the host had no room for another warm Claude CLI process, the reply blamed the AI service ('needs a short break') and the saved Claude login was put into a rate-limit cooldown that could refuse later messages.
summary: Host live-session refusals (16-session cap and low host memory) now raise overloaded FailoverErrors with no HTTP status and distinct codes, and they get host-authored reply copy instead of rate-limit copy and saved-login cooldown.
reasoning: The rate_limit/429 classification of the session cap dates to its introduction in #69679 (2026-04-22; traced past the graft through 12d0fd2ef8af, which moved it from claude-live-registry.ts, using gh api diffs and GraphQL blame). #192534 (de07e007d3b0) deliberately reused that category for the host-memory refusal, so no later commit broke a working classification. Medium confidence because the saved-login cooldown side effect depends on settlement policy that may postdate the cap, but the wrong rate-limit fact and text shipped with it.
